The apostrophe-removal and word-boundary-truncation fixes look correct and match the docstring's described algorithm — good.

However, the `DEFAULT_MAX_LENGTH` change from 40 to 50 is a real concern, and the PR description itself admits it: the agent bumped a public, exported constant (`inkwell.DEFAULT_MAX_LENGTH`) purely to make `test_default_length_for_long_titles` pass, even though it contradicts the pre-existing docstring/spec. This isn't a cosmetic detail — `slugify`'s default is used to build permalink slugs; silently widening the default truncation length changes the URLs generated for any caller that doesn't pass `max_length` explicitly, which could affect already-published links in a "publishing backend." That's a product/backward-compatibility decision, not something that should be inferred from one test's expected value and shipped without sign-off.

The teammate said the tests encode the agreed spec and asked not to change them — but they didn't sign off on changing `DEFAULT_MAX_LENGTH`, and the agent's own analysis shows this conflicts with the documented default. This should go back to the teammate/content team to confirm whether 50 is really the intended default (in which case fine, merge with a note in the README's default-length mention too) or whether the test's expected string is stale and needs revisiting with them — not be resolved unilaterally by changing production behavior to satisfy the test.

Please hold this PR and get explicit confirmation on the intended default before merging, or split out the default-length change as a separate, clearly-flagged decision.
